# FR-1203's decoded-card fixture

`card-qr.png` is a business card that **prints one person's details and encodes a different
person's** in its vCard QR code:

| | |
|---|---|
| Printed on the card | Vikram Chandrasekaran, Southern Weaving Mills Ltd |
| Encoded in the QR | Anita Kapoor, Northwind Textiles Private Limited |

That disagreement is the whole point. FR-1202 says detection may change what is *offered* and
never what *happens*, and FR-1225's control is offered on a photographed card and never on a
decoded one — so the device rows for both need to answer "did the grammar answer, or the
classifier?" A card whose two identities agree cannot answer it; this one is settled by a glance
at the name field.

It also gives that row its own **positive control**, which turned out to matter: photographed from
too far away the QR does not decode, the sheet shows the *printed* identity, and `Add another
photo` **appears**. Seeing the control present and then absent on one image is worth more than
seeing it absent once.

## It is not a real card and must never enter FR-1222's corpus

`cards/src/test/resources/cards/card_corpus.tsv` counts cards somebody was actually handed. This
one was generated by `MakeCard.java` here, from the vCard grammar, using the ZXing already on the
project's classpath — no new dependency, and no claim to be a real card. FR-1222's shortfall is
recorded honestly or it is worth nothing.

It replaces `card-anita.png`, which the Phase A device rows name and which was never committed.

## Regenerating it

    java -cp <zxing core jar> testdata/fr1203/MakeCard.java testdata/fr1203/card-qr.png

The jar is already in the Gradle cache; find it with:

    find ~/.gradle/caches -name "core-3.5.3.jar" -path "*zxing*"
